newsitem.title: UK: Catholic man wounded in N.Irish gun attack.
newsitem.headline: Catholic man wounded in N.Irish gun attack.

text.p: A gunman disguised as a postman wounded a Catholic man waiting for an early morning lift to work on the outskirts of Belfast on Wednesday.
Northern Ireland police said they had not yet established a motive but the political arm of IRA guerrillas blamed pro-British Protestant extremists.
A police spokesman said Kieran Delaney, 23, was approached by a man dressed as a postman "who produced a pistol from his postbag and fired a single shot, striking his victim on the neck".

"This morning's shooting bears all the hallmarks of a sectarian attack. I would urge people to remain calm and vigilant in the days ahead," said Gerry Kelly, a spokesman for the Irish Republican Army's political wing, Sinn Fein.

"We are certainly treating it as attempted murder," a police source said after the shooting near the northern suburb of Newtownabbey. Media reports said the victim narrowly missed death because the attacker's weapon jammed.
A car was later found partially burnt out close to a Protestant estate near the scene. Police said the vehicle and items found in it would be forensically examined.

Protestant and Catholic guerrillas who struck in rival areas during a bitter conflict that re-started last year have frequently torched getaway vehicles in their power-bases to destroy forensic traces.

The wounded man's father said his son had no political links and had been singled out because of his religion. Minority Catholics want British sovereignty to end and the region united with neighbouring Catholic Ireland.
Northern Ireland has suffered an upswing in hostilities over recent months by extremists who draw support in Catholic and Protestant districts.
The IRA, fighting to end British rule, has killed two British soldiers in the province since last October.
It has also set off bombs on mainland Britain. IRA bomb hoaxes last Saturday forced a two-day postponement of Britain's annual Grand National horse race near the city of Liverpool.

Protestant "Loyalist" guerrillas, pledged to fight to retain British rule, have been blamed for killing two Northern Ireland Catholics since last July. Their leaders insist, however, that a truce called in October 1994 is still in force.
A spate of arson attacks on Protestant and Catholic church property has intensfied tension in the province.
